root_cause.text: The UFS RTC delayed work (ufs_rtc_update_work) was not cancelled before the suspend path began clock gating and other power operations, creating a race where the work could attempt to access the hardware after it was partially suspended, triggering an SError.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states that cancel_delayed_work_sync() was placed after ufshcd_vops_suspend(POST_CHANGE), allowing ufshcd_rtc_work() to run concurrently with clock gating. The fix moves cancellation before ufshcd_vops_suspend(PRE_CHANGE) to ensure the work is fully completed or cancelled before any suspend operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel the RTC update work synchronously during UFS host suspend to avoid interference with the suspend sequence.
intent_record.what: Added a call to cancel_delayed_work_sync for hba->ufs_rtc_update_work after flushing eeh_work and before calling ufshcd_vops_suspend in __ufshcd_wl_suspend.
intent_record.how: This ensures any pending or executing RTC update work is fully stopped before the UFS host enters suspend, preventing potential races or access to hardware that may be powered down.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove cancellation of RTC update work during suspend to prevent potential synchronization issues or races.
intent_record.what: Removed the line `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work);` from the function `__ufshcd_wl_suspend`.
intent_record.how: Previously, when the function reached the `goto out;` path (successful execution before that point), it would synchronously cancel the RTC update work. After this change, that cancellation no longer occurs during this suspend path.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by cancelling the RTC update work synchronously before the suspend sequence, preventing the race condition.

The group removes cancellation of RTC update work during suspend, which is the opposite of the required fix. The vulnerability is caused by not cancelling the work before suspend, so removing cancellation would exacerbate the race condition.

candidates.rationale: This statement initiates the suspend sequence (including clock gating) without first cancelling the RTC update work, allowing a race condition where the work may access hardware after partial suspend, causing an SError.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement begins the suspend sequence (including clock gating) without first cancelling the RTC update work (ufs_rtc_update_work). The RTC work may subsequently attempt to access UFS hardware after it is partially suspended, causing a race condition that leads to an SError.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function ufshcd_suspend (starting at line 8773) does not include any cancellation of the UFS RTC delayed work (ufs_rtc_update_work) before performing clock gating and other power operations. For example, at line 8845, only 'eeh_work' is flushed; there is no equivalent 'cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work)'. This missing cancellation allows the work to race with suspend, matching the root cause described.
